statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is the unique integer declared winner by the following deterministic process. A position consists of a list q of the same integers as arr, a champion c, and a count w. Initially q=arr, c=arr[0], w=0. In each round, let x=q[0] and y=q[1], and let z be the larger of x and y. Replace q by the list whose first element is z, followed by q[2], q[3], ..., q[len(q)-1] (this middle part is empty when len(q)=2), followed by the smaller of x and y. If z=c then set w=w+1; otherwise set c=z and w=1. The first round at which w=k declares its current c to be the winner; r is that c. This process reaches such a declaration under the preconditions.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, and 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: For every arr and k satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and does not fail, panic, perform an out-of-bounds access, or overflow.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, and 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = max(arr[0], arr[1]).
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, 1 <= k <= 1000000000, and k=1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = arr[0].
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, 1 <= k <= 1000000000, and arr[0] > arr[i] for every i with 0 < i < len(arr).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the maximum element of arr.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, 1 <= k <= 1000000000, and k >= len(arr) - 1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= arr[0] and r >= arr[1].
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, and 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(arr) such that arr[i] = r.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, and 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(arr) such that arr[i] = r and, for every j with 0 <= j < i, arr[j] < r.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, and 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let i be the unique index with arr[i]=r and let m be the unique index with arr[m] equal to the maximum element of arr. If r is not the maximum element of arr, then i < m.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, and 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: For every two integers k1 and k2 with 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= 1000000000, if the function returns r1 on (arr, k1) and r2 on (arr, k2), and i1, i2 are the unique indices with arr[i1]=r1 and arr[i2]=r2, then i1 <= i2.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, and 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = arr[0] if and only if either (1) arr[i] < arr[0] for every i with 0 < i < len(arr), or (2) there exists an index p with 0 < p < len(arr) such that arr[p] > arr[0], arr[i] < arr[0] for every i with 0 < i < p, and k <= p - 1.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, and 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = arr[len(arr)-1].
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, 1 <= k <= 1000000000, k >= 2, and arr[i] < arr[i+1] for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1.

statement: For any valid array arr' with len(arr') >= 2, pairwise distinct elements between 1 and 1000000, arr'[0]=arr[0], and arr'[1]=arr[1], if the function returns r on (arr,1) and r' on (arr',1), then r=r'.
preconditions: arr and arr' are arrays with 2 <= len(arr) <= 100000 and 2 <= len(arr') <= 100000, every element of each is an integer between 1 and 1000000, the elements of each array are pairwise distinct, arr'[0]=arr[0], arr'[1]=arr[1], and k=1.

statement: Call an index i a prefix maximum if arr[i] > arr[j] for every 0 <= j < i. For such i, define run(i) as follows. Let p be the least index with i < p < len(arr) and arr[p] > arr[i], if it exists. If i=0 and such p exists, run(0)=p-1; if i>0 and such p exists, run(i)=p-i; if no such p exists, then arr[i] is the global maximum and run(i) is unbounded above every allowed k. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = arr[i] for the least prefix-maximum index i with run(i) >= k. This gives an equivalent non-simulating characterization of the answer.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2, len(arr) <= 100000, every element of arr is an integer with 1 <= arr[i] <= 1000000, the elements of arr are pairwise distinct, and 1 <= k <= 1000000000.
